## The problem

::: {.middle}
::: {.indent}
In 2024, LLMs were great with language, but shaky with simple math.
:::

> Which is bigger: 9.11 or 9.9?

::: {.indent}
GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Llama 3 (2024): **9.11** [✗]{style="color: red;"}
:::
:::

::: aside
[Jim Fan, X, July 2024](https://x.com/DrJimFan/status/1816521330298356181)
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 60%;"}
Chain of Code tested GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and PaLM 2.
:::

:::: {.columns style="display: block; margin-top: 2em;"}
::: {.column .small-text width="50%"}
[Chain of Thought]{.method-header} (Wei et al., 2022)

- Prompt shows worked examples, reasoning in words
- Model does the math itself, in text
:::

::: {.column .small-text width="50%"}
[Program of Thoughts]{.method-header} (Chen et al., 2022)

- Prompt shows worked examples, solved in Python
- Model writes code; Python runs it
- Fails if a step can't be written as code
:::
::::

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 60%;"}
Both were just few-shot prompts, with no extra training.
:::

[Logos: Wikimedia Commons (public domain)](https://commons.wikimedia.org/)

## Three Prompts to Answer "How Many Countries" {.small-title}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/prompt-direct-answer.png)

::: {.small-text}
[Direct Answer]{.method-header}

- Model answers immediately, no reasoning
- Right only 10%
:::

![](images/prompt-chain-of-thought.png)

::: {.small-text}
[Chain-of-Thought]{.method-header}

- Model reasons step-by-step in words
- Still right only 10%
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/prompt-chain-of-code.png)

::: {.small-text}
[Chain-of-Code]{.method-header}

- Prompt includes pseudo-code examples
- Model writes code to solve it
- Lines in red evaluated with Python
- Lines in purple: the LMulator (the LLM pretends to be Python)
- **Right 100% of the time**
:::
:::
::::

::: aside
[Figure 1 from Li et al., ICML 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04474)
:::

## Chain-of-Code Outperforms Direct-Answer and Chain-of-Thought {.smaller-title}

![](images/figure-2-results.png)

::: {.small-text}
BIG-Bench Hard: 23 tasks that are hard for LLMs. Examples:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Arithmetic:** ((−3 + 5 × 8 × −4) − (9 − 8 × −7)) = ?
- **Brackets:** close the sequence ( [ { } ]
- **Dates:** what date was 10 days before Christmas Eve 1937?
- **Logic:** not (True and False) or False = ?
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Word order:** "terrible rubber ship" or "rubber terrible ship"?
- **Sports:** is "the quarterback hit a home run" plausible?
- **Sarcasm:** which of two sentences is sarcastic?
:::
::::
:::

::: aside
[Figure 2 from Li et al., ICML 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04474)
:::

> Of the birthdays of Banting, Curie, Darwin, Einstein, Gauss, Hawking, Lovelace, Rutherford, Tesla, and Turing that are at least 100 days before or after **15 March 2027**, whose is closest?

## Impact of Chain of Code

::: {.middle .side-logos style="font-size: 85%;"}
- Oral presentation at ICML 2024
- Cited by 200+ papers
- Follow-up work on when to write code vs. reason in words (Chen et al., ICLR 2025) ![](images/logo-iclr.svg){.side-logo}
- Models are now trained to reason step by step on their own, without few-shot prompts
- Today's reasoning models run code in the middle of their reasoning (OpenAI o3, 2025) ![](images/logo-openai.png){.side-logo}
:::

::: aside
[Citations: Google Scholar, Oct 2026](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Chain+of+Code%3A+Reasoning+with+a+Language+Model-Augmented+Code+Emulator%22) · [OpenAI o3, Apr 2025](https://openai.com/index/introducing-o3-and-o4-mini/) · Logos: [iclr.cc](https://iclr.cc/), [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/)
:::

## Summary and Conclusion

::: {.middle style="font-size: 85%;"}
- LLMs know facts, but are shaky at exact math
- Chain of Code: the LLM writes code; Python runs what it can, the LLM emulates the rest
- Paper: 84% on BIG-Bench Hard, vs. 72% for Chain of Thought
- Our demo (7B model): 100% vs. 10%, with the same facts, but Python doing the math
- Limitations:
  - works best when the examples come from the same kind of problem
  - requires prompt engineering (using models at the time)
:::
